title: First return of the comparator
statement: Let $w,u,v$ be Boolean words and let $p$ be a valid input-head position for input $w$. There is an integer $t$ with $0<t\le 2(\max(|u|,|v|)+1)$ such that, at every time $j<t$, the comparator is in neither of its return states, and after $t$ steps it is in its return phase with its register equal to the truth value of $u=v$, both word-tape heads at zero, and its other configuration data as initially specified.
replaced:
For words $u, v$, there is a time $t$ with
$0 < t \le 2(\max(\abs{u},\abs{v}) + 1)$ such that the comparator never
visits either Boolean return state before time $t$ and at time $t$ sits in
its return configuration with the register recording whether $u = v$ and
both heads at zero.
